sections.heading: Describing personality
sections.body:
Personality is what someone is like — use *ser*: *Mi jefa es muy trabajadora y un poco seria.* Useful words: *amable* (kind), *simpático* (nice), *antipático* (unpleasant), *divertido* (fun), *serio* (serious), *tímido* (shy), *extrovertido*, *trabajador* (hard-working), *perezoso / flojo* (lazy), *generoso*, *tacaño* (stingy), *honesto*, *mentiroso* (lying), *paciente*, *impaciente*, *tranquilo* (calm), *nervioso* (a nervous person).

To soften a criticism: *Es un poco…* or *No es muy…*: *No es muy paciente.*

sections.heading: Adjectives that change meaning with ser and estar
sections.body: Some adjectives mean different things depending on the verb:

head: Adjective
with ser (what someone is like)
with estar (state now)
rows: *Está malo* — he's ill (or the food has gone bad)

sections.heading: Physical description (people)
sections.body: *Es alto / bajo / delgado* (thin) */ gordito* (chubby — *gordo* can be blunt) */ guapo* (good-looking) */ moreno* (dark-haired or dark-skinned) */ rubio*. *Tiene el pelo…, los ojos…*. *Lleva lentes / barba / bigote* (mustache). Age: *Es joven / mayor. Tiene unos cuarenta años* (about forty).

examples: Mi jefa es muy trabajadora y un poco seria.
My boss is very hard-working and a bit serious.
Mi hermano es divertido y muy generoso.
My brother is fun and very generous.
El niño está malo; tiene fiebre.
The boy is ill; he has a fever.
He has a mustache and wears glasses.
Mi abuela es una persona muy amable.
My grandmother is a very kind person.
¿Cómo es tu novio? Es guapo y muy simpático.
What's your boyfriend like? He's handsome and very nice.
My father has a strong personality.
